papers.title: The Mirage of Optimizing Training Policies: Monotonic Inference Policies as the Real Objective for LLM Reinforcement Learning

summary.tldr: This paper introduces Monotonic Inference Policy Improvement (MIPI) and Monotonic Inference Policy Update (MIPU) to address objective misalignment in LLM RL, improving reasoning performance and training stability under training-inference mismatch.
key_points: LLM RL suffers from training-inference mismatch, where separate engines exhibit inconsistent probabilities for the same trajectories, leading to off-policyness.
Existing works address off-policyness, but neglect objective misalignment where training policy updates don't guarantee inference policy improvement.
MIPI is proposed as a new policy optimization objective for LLM RL, focusing on monotonic improvement of the inference policy.
MIPU is a two-step LLM RL framework that generates sampler-referenced candidate updates and selectively accepts synchronized candidates using an inference-side gap proxy.
Experiments on two model scales with high mismatch show MIPU improves average reasoning performance and training stability.
summary.why_it_matters: Addressing training-inference mismatch and objective misalignment can lead to more stable and effective reinforcement learning for large language models.

papers.title: Embodied.cpp: A Portable Inference Runtime of Embodied AI Models on Heterogeneous Robots

summary.tldr: Embodied.cpp is a portable C++ inference runtime designed for deploying embodied AI models on heterogeneous robots, addressing limitations of existing runtimes for multi-rate, latency-first, batch-1 inference.
key_points: Embodied.cpp organizes the shared execution path of VLA models and WAMs into five layers: input adapters, sequence builders, backbone execution, head plugins, and deployment adapters.
The runtime supports modular multi-rate execution, latency-first fused inference, and extensible operator/I/O, enabling deployment across heterogeneous devices, robots, and simulators.
Evaluated on HY-VLA and pi0.5 VLA models, Embodied.cpp achieved 100.0% and 91.0% task success rates in closed-loop execution.
A WAM benchmark using a LingBot-VA Transformer block showed Embodied.cpp reduced block memory from 312.2 MiB to 88.1 MiB.
summary.why_it_matters: This runtime provides a unified solution for deploying complex embodied AI models efficiently on diverse robotic hardware, overcoming fragmentation and performance issues of current methods.

papers.title: DataComp-VLM: Improved Open Datasets for Vision-Language Models

summary.tldr: DataComp for VLMs (DCVLM) is a new benchmark for evaluating data curation strategies for Vision-Language Models, featuring 160 datasets and 6T multimodal tokens.
key_points: DCVLM integrates 160 datasets across four types: image-caption pairs, multimodal interleaved documents, text-only, and instruction-tuning data, totaling 6T multimodal tokens.
The benchmark supports testing data curation strategies (filtering, mixing, formatting, sampling) on 1B-8B models with 6.25B-200B token budgets.
Evaluation uses a suite of up to 52 downstream benchmarks across 9 domains.
Experiments show data mixing, particularly instruction-heavy mixtures, is more effective than filtering for VLM training, with gains increasing at larger scales.
The resulting DCVLM-Baseline dataset enables an 8B VLM to achieve 63.6% accuracy on a 33-task core suite with 200B training tokens, a +5.4pp improvement over FineVision.
summary.why_it_matters: This benchmark provides a systematic method to improve VLM training datasets, leading to more performant open VLMs.

papers.title: OrbitQuant: Data-Agnostic Quantization for Image and Video Diffusion Transformers

summary.tldr: OrbitQuant introduces a data-agnostic weight-activation quantizer for Diffusion Transformers, using a normalized, rotated basis to enable consistent quantization across varying inputs and modalities.
key_points: OrbitQuant quantizes in a normalized, rotated basis, bypassing range estimation challenges caused by shifting DiT activations across timesteps, prompts, and guidance branches.

A randomized permuted block-Hadamard (RPBH) rotation concentrates coordinates around a fixed marginal, allowing a single Lloyd-Max codebook to serve all timesteps, prompts, and layers for a given input dimension.
Weight rows are quantized offline, absorbing the rotation into the weights to cancel within linear layers, leaving only a forward rotation on activations at runtime.
The method transfers from image to video diffusion transformers without per-modality tuning.
OrbitQuant achieves state-of-the-art PTQ on FLUX.1, Z-Image-Turbo, Wan 2.1, and CogVideoX, enabling usable W2A4 PTQ for image diffusion transformers.
summary.why_it_matters: This method significantly reduces inference costs for state-of-the-art image and video generation models by enabling efficient post-training quantization without extensive recalibration.

papers.title: VLA-Corrector: Lightweight Detect-and-Correct Inference for Adaptive Action Horizon

summary.tldr: VLA-Corrector introduces a detect-and-correct framework for action-chunked VLA policies, using a Latent-space Vision Monitor (LVM) to detect visual deviations and trigger replanning via Online Gradient Guidance (OGG), enabling an adaptive action horizon.
key_points: VLA-Corrector integrates a Latent-space Vision Monitor (LVM) to continuously compare predicted and actual visual feature evolution.
Upon detection of persistent visual dynamics deviation, VLA-Corrector triggers a truncation event, discarding remaining actions.
Corrective replanning is invoked via Online Gradient Guidance (OGG) when a deviation is detected.
The system induces an event-triggered adaptive action horizon, preserving long-horizon execution when reliable and invoking short-horizon replanning when drift occurs.
VLA-Corrector can be integrated into existing VLA models without retraining the backbone policy weights.
summary.why_it_matters: This method improves robustness in long-horizon, contact-rich robotic manipulation tasks by mitigating compounding errors while retaining efficiency benefits of action chunking.

papers.title: Measuring the Gap Between Human and LLM Research Ideas

summary.tldr: A new framework evaluates the gap between human and LLM-generated research ideas by reverse-engineering prior works and using a two-axis research-taste taxonomy.
key_points: A large-scale evaluation framework was built to compare LLM-generated ideas with human research papers.
The framework reverse-engineers closely related prior works that likely inspired core ideas in human papers.
LLMs generate new ideas from sets of paper titles and summaries.
A two-axis research-taste taxonomy profiles ideas by opportunity pattern and research paradigm to quantify divergence.
LLM ideas disproportionately concentrate on bridge-like opportunities and synthesis methods, unlike the broader distribution of human ideas.
summary.why_it_matters: This research identifies systematic differences in ideation patterns between LLMs and humans, informing future development of AI research assistants.

papers.title: Securing the AI Agent: A Unified Framework for Multi-Layer Agent Red Teaming

summary.tldr: AI-Infra-Guard is an open-source framework for multi-layer AI agent red teaming, addressing the stratified attack surface across infrastructure, protocol/tool, agent behavior, and model layers with distinct detection paradigms.
key_points: AI-Infra-Guard organizes AI red teaming by matching specific detection paradigms to each of four distinct layers: infrastructure, protocol/tool, agent behavior, and model.
The framework includes deterministic rule matching for over 75 AI components and 1,400 vulnerability rules at the infrastructure layer.
It employs LLM-driven agentic auditing for Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers and agent-skill packages.
Multi-turn black-box agent red teaming is used for agent behavior, and a jailbreak harness with 26+ attack operators across sixteen datasets targets the model layer.
summary.why_it_matters: This framework provides a practical, unified, and open-source foundation for securing AI agents by systematically addressing their complex, multi-layered attack surface.

papers.title: MultAttnAttrib: Training-Free Multimodal Attribution in Long Document Question Answering

summary.tldr: MultAttnAttrib is a training-free multimodal attribution method for long document QA, leveraging prefill pass, attention heads, and calibrated thresholds to locate source evidence, outperforming existing methods and matching frontier models like GPT 5.4.
key_points: MultAttnAttrib is a training-free method for multimodal attribution in long document question answering.
It utilizes a model's prefill pass, selected attention heads, and calibrated thresholds to identify source evidence.
MultAttrEval is a new benchmark dataset with fine-grained, ground-truth attributions for multimodal source documents.
MultAttnAttrib outperforms various attribution-generation methods, including prompting-based approaches, and matches GPT 5.4.
The method substantially improves attribution accuracy for both unimodal and multimodal types, reducing inference latency by up to seven times compared to prompting.
summary.why_it_matters: This method enhances user trust and model safety in grounded QA systems by accurately attributing generated answers to multimodal evidence with improved efficiency.

papers.title: AnyBokeh: Physics-Guided Any-to-Any Bokeh Editing with Optical Fingerprint Transfer

summary.tldr: AnyBokeh introduces a physics-guided framework for any-to-any bokeh editing by estimating source blur state and optical fingerprint, enabling relative blur synthesis without all-in-focus reconstruction.
key_points: AnyBokeh estimates the source blur state using a signed circle-of-confusion map and a disparity map.
It models the linear relation between signed circle of confusion and disparity difference to estimate a source-specific optical fingerprint.
A generative editor uses source and target circle-of-confusion maps for relative blur synthesis, allowing spatially adaptive deblurring, preservation, and defocus rendering.
A high-fidelity synthetic dataset with accurate depth, focus distance, and EXIF metadata was constructed for physically supervised learning.
summary.why_it_matters: This method enables faithful and controllable bokeh editing across various scenarios, avoiding common limitations of existing approaches like all-in-focus reconstruction and test-time calibration.

papers.title: Teaching LLMs to Recommend and Defer in Underrepresented Epilepsy Care

summary.tldr: MANANA, a non-parametric prompt-learning framework, improves LLM-based anti-seizure medication recommendations in Ugandan pediatric epilepsy care by learning local prescribing guidance and enabling uncertainty-based deferral.
key_points: Standard LLM prompting for anti-seizure medication recommendations shows errors due to distribution-miscalibrated prescribing defaults, not parsing failures.
MANANA converts observed prescription errors into auditable prompt memories, improving over classical ML, direct LLM prompting, and prompt-optimization baselines.
Bayesian prompt averaging converts learned prompt trajectories into prescription likelihoods and an uncertainty-based deferral signal.
The system achieves 4-8 percentage point improvement in visit-level top-3 prescription accuracy on an independent cohort.
Selective prediction allows auto-handling 50% of cases at 95% precision or 25% at 99% precision, deferring lower-confidence cases.
summary.why_it_matters: This system can enhance epilepsy care in resource-constrained settings by providing accurate, locally-adapted medication recommendations and identifying cases requiring specialist review.

papers.title: Generated Contents Enrichment

summary.tldr: A new adversarial framework enriches sparse scene descriptions by explicitly modeling object semantics and inter-object relations via scene graphs before image generation.
key_points: Generated Contents Enrichment (GCE) is proposed, focusing on explicit scene representation enrichment before rendering.
The framework uses graph convolutional networks to predict additional objects and relations, enriching an initial scene graph.
Enriched scene graphs are then passed to an image-generation pipeline to produce visually plausible and coherent content.
Evaluation includes proxy scene graph enrichment metrics, image-quality comparisons, and user studies on the Visual Genome dataset.
summary.why_it_matters: This approach enables more controllable and semantically richer image generation from limited textual inputs by making the enrichment process explicit.

papers.title: AGE: Adaptive-masking for Graph Embedding in Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation

summary.tldr: AGE introduces an Adaptive-masking for Graph Embedding method using a Transformer and mask-based self-supervised learning to align graph-based and text-based latent features for GraphRAG with frozen LLMs.
key_points: AGE addresses misalignment between graph-based and text-based latent features in GraphRAG for frozen LLMs.
It employs a Transformer in a mask-based self-supervised learning (SSL) approach, designed similar to text embedding encoders.
AGE utilizes a learnable node sampler to predict nodes apart from "key nodes" to improve SSL efficiency.
Experimental results show AGE significantly improves non-parametric search in GraphQA tasks, achieving superior accuracy across four benchmark datasets.
summary.why_it_matters: This method enhances the ability of LLMs to effectively utilize graph-structured data as external knowledge, improving GraphRAG performance.

papers.title: Interpretation-Oriented Cloud Removal via Observation-Anchored Residual Flow with Geo-Contextual Alignment

summary.tldr: Geo-Anchored Cloud Removal (GACR) is a unified framework for cloud removal that ensures faithful reconstruction and robust interpretability by incorporating Observation-Anchored Residual Flow and Geo-Contextual Prior Alignment.
key_points: GACR reformulates cloud removal as a physically grounded residual inversion process using Observation-Anchored Residual Flow (OAR-Flow).
OAR-Flow anchors the generative trajectory to the cloudy observation, enabling fast, stable, and faithful reconstruction.
GACR integrates Geo-Contextual Prior Alignment (GCPA) to constrain reconstruction within a semantic manifold induced by a Vision Foundation Model (VFM).
GACR maintains spatial-semantic integrity, improving downstream task accuracy across six datasets and twelve tasks.
Code for GACR is available at https://github.com/wzy6055/GACR.
summary.why_it_matters: GACR addresses semantic drift and degraded downstream performance in cloud removal, making it more suitable for reliable interpretation in optical remote sensing.

papers.title: Memory in the Loop: In-Process Retrieval as Extended Working Memory for Language Agents

summary.tldr: In-process memory, with ~100us latency, enables language agents to integrate retrieval directly into their observe-reason-act loop, significantly reducing redundant actions and improving recall compared to traditional networked memory stores.
key_points: In-process memory stores achieve ~100us latency, three orders of magnitude faster than networked stores.
Integrating memory into the agent's loop (read/write on every step) reduces redundant actions from 7.2 of 12 (110ms cloud latency) to 0.0 of 12 (in-process speed).
Recall improved from 0/5 to 3.6-4.8/5 across four GPT-5-class models with in-loop memory, with store operations at p50 80-165us.
The dominant per-step cost shifts from memory retrieval to embedding (~200-400ms over network), which can be reduced to ~40us with a local embedder.
The in-process store maintained 100% fact retention (244 of 244 writes kept); all misses were due to agent's read policy.
summary.why_it_matters: This approach allows language agents to leverage memory as extended working memory, enabling more efficient and effective reasoning by eliminating latency-induced bottlenecks.

papers.title: FirstResearch: Auditable Question Formation for LLM Scientific Discovery Agents

summary.tldr: FirstResearch introduces a framework for auditable research question formation in scientific LLM agents, utilizing a structured Research Question Certificate to expose underlying mechanisms and assumptions.
key_points: FirstResearch employs a Research Question Certificate, detailing primitive definitions, assumptions, a mechanism model, tension, falsifiable hypothesis, minimal decisive test, and failure update rule.
On ten LLM-agent research topics, FirstResearch scored 4.86/5 against a 4.38/5 baseline using a DeepSeek-blind-judge protocol.
A Gemini-2.5-Flash independent-judge rescore confirmed the system-level ranking, with FirstResearch at 4.86/5 and the strongest baseline at 4.38/5, showing 0.865 Pearson agreement.
Ablation studies indicate the certificate-centered core is critical, with certificate-only scoring 4.90/5 (DeepSeek) and 4.88/5 (Gemini), while removing certificates dropped scores below 1/5.
summary.why_it_matters: This framework enhances the inspectability and trustworthiness of research questions generated by LLM scientific discovery agents, facilitating better scientific scrutiny.

papers.title: RPAM: A Principled Metric for Evaluating Associations in Language Models with High Predictive Validity in Downstream Outputs

summary.tldr: RPAM is a new upstream metric for generative language models that strongly correlates with human and downstream associations, outperforming previous methods.
key_points: RPAM (Relative Probability Association Metric) is an upstream evaluation metric for generative language models.
RPAM measures associations at the fundamental level of embeddings or continuation probabilities.
RPAM demonstrates a strong relationship with implicit and explicit human associations and downstream biases across Mistral-7B-Instruct, Mistral-7B, and GPT-2.
Evaluated on WEAT-WS, Bellezza, WS-353, and SST2 datasets, RPAM outperforms prior record values in correlating with real-world associations.
summary.why_it_matters: This metric provides a more accurate and generalizable method for evaluating and mitigating problematic biases in language models.

papers.title: When Agents Remember Too Much: Memory Poisoning Attacks on Large Language Model Agents

summary.tldr: A novel attack, GhostWriter, exploits memory subsystems in LLM agents, achieving 98% injection and 60% activation rates, mitigated by Agentic Memory Sentry (AM-Sentry) using memory-saving policies and retrieval screening.
key_points: GhostWriter is a two-phase memory poisoning attack: injection (adversary sends hidden payload) and activation (poisoned memory retrieved).
GhostWriter achieves approximately 98% injection rates and 60% average activation rates against state-of-the-art agents.
The attack targets personal AI agents with long-term memory, particularly those at the convergence of conversational and action-planning domains.
AM-Sentry mitigates GhostWriter using a memory-saving policy and a memory-retrieval screen.
The vulnerability stems from a lack of security-focused memory governance in current agent designs.
summary.why_it_matters: This attack highlights critical security vulnerabilities in personal AI agents that handle sensitive information and interact with untrusted sources, necessitating robust memory governance.

papers.title: ResonatorLM: Causal Resonant Field Mixing for Efficient Long-Context Language Modeling

summary.tldr: ResonatorLM replaces transformer self-attention with causal functions of damped resonators, treating token sequences as a driven one-dimensional latent field for efficient long-context language modeling.
key_points: ResonatorLM replaces the attention mechanism in transformers with a physics-derived alternative based on causal functions of damped resonators.
It models token sequences as a single, driven one-dimensional latent field.
In a 6M matched setting, ResonatorLM achieves a 6.47x decode speedup compared to optimized transformers at 32K tokens.
ResonatorLM demonstrates 61.31% accuracy on WikiText, surpassing the 55.32% of standard transformers.
summary.why_it_matters: This new architecture offers significant speedups and improved accuracy for processing long contexts, addressing a key limitation of current transformer models.

papers.title: AIR-BENCH Live: An Evolving Safety Benchmark for Foundation Models

summary.tldr: AIR-BENCH Live is an evolving safety benchmark for foundation models that automatically updates risk taxonomies from government regulations and generates new multilingual prompts to maintain relevance.
key_points: AIR-BENCH Live expands from 314 to 335 granular risks, incorporating 21 new categories from 31 novel policy clauses across seven jurisdictions.
An automated update pipeline monitors government regulation, classifying new policies against a four-tier risk taxonomy or proposing new granular categories.
A multi-agent, persona-driven algorithm generates realistic, multilingual prompts, overhauling legacy prompts and creating new ones for new categories.
Modernized prompts are 0.06 points harder than the 2024 set, with the largest safety drops observed in the most compliant models.
Evaluation of 14 recent models shows a safety spread from 0.17 to 0.89 and models are modestly less safe on non-English prompts.
summary.why_it_matters: This benchmark provides a continuously updated and more robust method for evaluating the safety of foundation models against evolving AI risks and regulations.

papers.title: MetaSkill-Evolve: Recursive Self-Improvement of LLM Agents via Two-Timescale Meta-Skill Evolution

summary.tldr: MetaSkill-Evolve introduces recursive self-improvement for LLM agents by evolving both task skills and meta-skills across two timescales, outperforming single-level evolution baselines.
key_points: MetaSkill-Evolve uses a two-timescale framework where task skills (s) evolve on a fast loop and meta-skills (m) evolve on a slower loop.
The meta-skill m consists of five components (Analyzer, Retriever, Allocator, Proposer, Evolver agents) that parameterize the improvement pipeline.
The meta-skill evolves under the same improvement pipeline applied to itself, without additional models or objectives.
All five pipeline agents share a single frozen backbone.
MetaSkill-Evolve improved held-out test accuracy by +23.54 points on OfficeQA, +16.09 points on SealQA, and +1.92 points on ALFWorld compared to the raw backbone.
summary.why_it_matters: This recursive self-improvement allows LLM agents to adapt their learning process, leading to more robust and effective performance across diverse tasks.

papers.title: A Coin Flip Per Token: Bernoulli Sparse Steering of Large Language Models

summary.tldr: Stochastic Token Steering (STS) and Stochastic Block Steering (SBS) enable sparse activation steering in LLMs, recovering most dense-steering effects with 50% token intervention and outperforming prompt-based control with 30% intervention.
key_points: STS gates each token independently with probability p, while SBS gates a leading window once per sequence, both without reward models or learned gating policies.
Steering only 50% of tokens recovers most of the dense-steering effect while preserving fluency across two model families and two behavioral tasks.
Steering as few as 30% of tokens surpasses prompt-based control.
Optimal steering magnitude scales inversely with the intervention ratio, indicating behavioral outcome depends on cumulative signal dosage.
summary.why_it_matters: This method allows for efficient and fluent behavioral control of large language models without constant per-token perturbation, reducing the risk of fluency degradation.

papers.title: CompactionRL: Reinforcement Learning with Context Compaction for Long-Horizon Agents

summary.tldr: CompactionRL is a reinforcement learning strategy that jointly optimizes task execution and summary generation for long-horizon agentic LLMs using context compaction.
key_points: CompactionRL incorporates context compaction into reinforcement learning for long-horizon agentic LLMs.
The approach jointly optimizes task execution and summary generation using token-level loss normalization and cross-trajectory generalized advantage estimation.
CompactionRL improved Pass@1 scores for GLM-4.5-Air (106B-A30B) by 7.0 points to 66.8% on SWE-bench Verified and 3.1 points to 24.5% on Terminal-Bench 2.0.
CompactionRL improved Pass@1 scores for GLM-4.7-Flash (30B-A3B) by 5.5 points to 56.0% on SWE-bench Verified and 6.8 points to 20.2% on Terminal-Bench 2.0.
CompactionRL is used in the RL pipeline for training the GLM-5.2 model (750B-A40B).
summary.why_it_matters: This method enables LLM agents to learn from compacted long-horizon trajectories, addressing limitations of finite context windows in extended interactions.

papers.title: Faithfulness to Refusal: A Causal Audit of Neuron Selectors

summary.tldr: This paper introduces a causal audit method for neuron selectors using one-shot neuron-row zeroing, demonstrating attribution methods' superiority in identifying causally important rows for both language modeling and installing refusal behaviors.
key_points: Attribution methods significantly outperform activation and magnitude-based baselines in identifying dispensable neuron rows across five LLMs at the language-modeling level.
The identified attributed rows are sufficient to install refusal on hate and crime while maintaining low benign over-refusal and preserving language model fluency.
Layer-matched random controls at the same depths fail to achieve the same refusal installation, indicating specificity of the attributed rows.
Highly rank-stable selectors can be causally invalid, highlighting a disconnect between rank-stability proxies and direct causal audits.
Refusal resides in a redundant subspace, with different attribution methods installing it via largely disjoint row sets, implying multiple sufficient mechanisms rather than a unique one.
summary.why_it_matters: Direct causal auditing of neuron selectors is crucial for reliable pruning, interpretability, and safety editing in large language models, as rank-stability metrics can be misleading.

papers.title: How Much is Left? LLMs Linearly Encode Their Remaining Output Length

summary.tldr: LLMs linearly encode their remaining output length, decodable from hidden states, suggesting an internal plan-like representation of response length.
key_points: Total response length is linearly decodable from the prompt's last hidden state before any output is generated.
Linear probes trained on natural-language datasets transfer to synthetic completions, outperforming a statistical baseline, while the reverse transfer fails.
On high-loss completions, the probe's per-position estimate shifts upward when the model retracts and restarts a partial solution.
summary.why_it_matters: This finding suggests LLMs maintain an internal representation of output length, which could inform future model design or analysis.

papers.title: Unified Audio Intelligence Without Regressing on Text Intelligence

summary.tldr: Nemotron-Labs-Audex-30B-A3B (Audex) is introduced as a unified audio-text LLM, built on Nemotron-Cascade-2-30B-A3B, demonstrating state-of-the-art audio capabilities without regressing on text intelligence.
key_points: Audex is a unified audio-text LLM based on the Nemotron-Cascade-2-30B-A3B text-only MoE LLM.
The architecture uses a single Transformer decoder where audio inputs are projected into the text embedding space, and text/quantized audio output tokens are treated uniformly.
Training involved 157.4B audio tokens and 320.5B text tokens, utilizing multi-stage supervised training, text-only Cascade RL, and multi-domain on-policy distillation.
Audex achieves state-of-the-art performance in audio understanding, speech recognition/translation, text-to-speech, audio generation, and speech-to-speech generation.
summary.why_it_matters: This model enables advanced multimodal generation and understanding while preserving the strong reasoning and knowledge capabilities of its text-only backbone.

papers.title: Weak-to-Strong Generalization via Direct On-Policy Distillation

summary.tldr: Direct-OPD transfers RL reasoning gains from weak to strong models by using the log-ratio between post-RL and pre-RL weak checkpoints as a dense implicit reward on student-generated states.
key_points: Uses the log-ratio of a weak model's post-RL and pre-RL checkpoints to isolate the RL-induced policy shift from the weak model's structural limitations.
Applies this policy shift signal as a dense implicit reward on the stronger target model's own on-policy states, avoiding sparse-reward RL on the target.
Boosted Qwen3-1.7B performance on AIME 2024 from 48.3% to 58.3% in 4 hours using 8 A100 GPUs.
Outperforms step-matched direct RL on the target model and allows sequential composition of multiple policy shifts.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables cheap, scalable post-training by allowing developers to run expensive RL rollouts on small models and directly transfer the learned policy improvements to larger models.

papers.title: TREK: Distill to Explore, Reinforce to Refine

summary.tldr: TREK uses teacher-guided forward-KL distillation to expand on-policy support on hard prompts before refining the policy with Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO).
key_points: Identifies low-pass-rate prompts and obtains verified candidate solutions from external black-box, white-box, or self-context teachers.
Filters candidate solutions by keeping the top-r proposals ranked by current student likelihood.
Applies a brief forward-KL distillation phase on filtered verified modes, then resumes standard on-policy GRPO refinement.
Improves Qwen3-8B AIME 2025 scores from 36.9 to 40.3 with DeepSeek-V4 proposals and to 38.5 using self-context proposals.
Boosts agentic task success rates on ALFWorld (75.8 to 82.8) and ScienceWorld (12.5 to 26.7), reaching high success on hard tasks earlier in training.
summary.why_it_matters: TREK prevents reinforcement learning from stalling on difficult prompts by efficiently expanding student model trajectory support using verified proposals without needing internal teacher access.

papers.title: Learning Only What Valid Adapters Can Express: Subspace-Constrained Adaptation Against Fine-Tuning Poisoning

summary.tldr: A novel parameter-efficient adaptation method constrains gradient updates to a low-dimensional subspace derived from trusted LoRA adapters, preventing fine-tuning poisoning while matching clean performance.
key_points: Analysis of 196 public LoRA adapters on flan-t5-large shows 30-38% of weight norm is redundant, confirming task updates lie in a shared low-dimensional subspace.

Restricting gradient updates to 128 coordinates of this subspace maintains clean classification performance while preserving 62-96% exact match accuracy under label inversion attacks, compared to 3-26% for standard LoRA.
The method produces a 120x adaptation loss gap between clean and corrupted data, providing inherently out-of-distribution detection without auxiliary models.

Against adaptive backdoor attacks within the subspace, attack success dropped to 8% (vs 100% for LoRA) on tasks unaligned with pool behaviors, though efficacy decreases if the attack target aligns with pool directions.
summary.why_it_matters: This approach provides built-in defense against fine-tuning poisoning and backdoor attacks for specialized downstream tasks without needing separate detector models.

papers.title: Multi-Turn On-Policy Distillation with Prefix Replay

summary.tldr: ReOPD replaces costly online environment interactions in multi-turn on-policy distillation by reusing pre-collected teacher trajectories as replayed prefixes with a step-decaying sampling schedule to avoid teacher target unreliability.
key_points: Identifies the 'prefix trap' in multi-turn OPD, where querying teachers on student-on-policy histories risks generating unreliable teacher targets.
Implements Replayed-Prefix On-Policy Distillation (ReOPD), an off-environment method using step-decaying sampling schedules to emphasize early, low-shift trajectory prefixes.
Eliminates tool calls during student training, reducing rollout runtime by at least 4x compared to standard OPD.
Evaluated on mathematical reasoning with Python and search environments across multiple student and teacher model scales while preserving or improving OPD accuracy.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables scalable, cost-effective agent distillation by converting expensive live environment interactions into a reusable offline training process without sacrificing model accuracy.

papers.title: LP-SFT: Local-Preserving Supervised Fine-Tuning via Multimodal Entropy Structure

summary.tldr: LP-SFT is a fine-tuning objective that preserves a pretrained model's multimodal entropy structure by enforcing a locally normalized KL divergence over non-label top-K tokens, preventing capability degradation while improving performance.
key_points: Shannon and Renyi entropy analyses reveal pretrained models possess a multimodal entropy structure with peaks representing varying numbers of plausible token alternatives.
Standard cross-entropy fine-tuning promotes only the ground-truth token, leaving the probability redistribution of unobserved alternative tokens unconstrained.
LP-SFT constructs a local top-K support set from the frozen base model, removes the target token to prevent optimization conflict, and applies locally normalized KL divergence to non-label tokens.
Evaluations show LP-SFT outperforms vanilla SFT and existing baselines across single- and mixed-domain tasks, optimizing the trade-off between pass@1 accuracy and pass@k diversity.
summary.why_it_matters: It prevents models from losing pre-existing capabilities and sampling diversity during domain-specific supervised fine-tuning.

papers.title: Turning Off-Policy Tokens On-Policy: A Plug-in Approach for Improving LLM Alignment

summary.tldr: Selective Importance Sampling (SIS) is a plug-in method that uses a token-level rejection test to convert off-policy tokens into on-policy tokens, reducing gradient variance in LLM reinforcement learning post-training.
key_points: Combines rejection sampling with importance sampling (IS) by treating the off-policy model as a proposal distribution.
Accepted tokens receive a unit importance score (treated as on-policy), while rejected tokens retain standard IS ratio corrections.
Theoretically reduces the gap between token-level and sequence-level off-policy gradient estimators without introducing significant wall-clock overhead.
Evaluated on dense and Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) LLMs using math and agent benchmarks.
summary.why_it_matters: SIS stabilizes long-sequence RL post-training for LLMs by preventing importance-ratio variance explosion while remaining compatible with existing RL algorithms.

papers.title: To Retain or to Adapt? Generalizing Continual Learning

summary.tldr: This paper challenges continual learning's focus on catastrophic forgetting, formalizing it via Average Lifelong Error and introducing a threshold where past knowledge transitions from a warm-start advantage to an optimization liability.
key_points: Formalizes continual learning via Average Lifelong Error (ALE) and introduces Transfer Efficiency to balance Instability (past bias) and Transient Error (learning from scratch).
Derives a closed-form Critical Task Duration threshold that identifies when retaining historical knowledge becomes an optimization hindrance under positive stationary bias.

Proposes Predictive Continual Learning, a framework optimizing future performance using an explicit task-drift model, instantiated by a Window algorithm that interpolates between Joint-Task and Independent-Task Learning.
summary.why_it_matters: It shifts continual learning paradigms from strict knowledge retention toward dynamic adaptation, preventing past data from impeding performance in shifting environments.

papers.title: Self-Review Reinforcement Learning (SRRL) with Cross-Episode Memory and Policy Distillation

summary.tldr: Self-Review Reinforcement Learning embeds policy-gradient-optimized self-reviews into RL episodes, internalizing corrections via selective distillation and reusing successful reviews across episodes using a cross-episode memory.
key_points: Embeds a self-review step into RL episodes when a first-pass response fails, conditioning an improved second attempt.
Optimizes self-reviews using policy gradients and internalizes corrections into the base policy through selective distillation to ensure cross-episode persistence.
Utilizes a cross-episode memory to store and reuse successful self-reviews when similar tasks are encountered during training.
Evaluated on the GSM8K benchmark using the GRPO optimizer with Qwen 3-4B and OLMo-3-7B models, outperforming standard RLVR in final reward and learning efficiency.
summary.why_it_matters: SRRL enables models to internalize past error corrections directly into their weights, improving learning efficiency in environments with sparse or delayed feedback.

papers.title: aiAuthZ: Off-Host, Identity-Bound Authorization for AI Agents

summary.tldr: aiAuthZ is an off-host authorization gateway that uses HMAC-SHA256 signatures, single-use nonces, and argument-level policies to reduce AI agent attack success to 0% with 0.03 ms added decision latency.
key_points: Evaluated 15 LLMs against eight real-world attack scenarios, revealing refusal rates varying from 100% down to 38%.
Uses per-message HMAC-SHA256 signatures bound to a single-use nonce, timestamp window, and immutable argument-level policies, alongside SHA-256 hash-chained audit logs.
Generates HMAC-authenticated QR receipts achieving 94% mean verification across eight channels with zero forgeries in 25 wrong-key trials.
Blocked 9 of 9 in-scope incident case studies and all 7 attacker-directed tool calls in the AgentDojo banking suite, outperforming a spotlighting baseline.
summary.why_it_matters: It prevents compromised or deceived AI agents from executing unauthorized tool calls by enforcing strict, identity-bound access controls off the agent's host.

papers.title: LLM-as-a-Verifier: A General-Purpose Verification Framework

summary.tldr: LLM-as-a-Verifier is a general-purpose, training-free verification framework that computes continuous solution scores by taking the expectation over scoring token logit distributions for agentic tasks.
key_points: Replaces discrete scoring prompts with continuous scores computed via the expectation over the distribution of scoring token logits.
Scales verification performance along three axes: score granularity for better class separation, repeated evaluation for variance reduction, and criteria decomposition for complexity reduction.
Includes a cost-efficient ranking algorithm to select optimal candidate solutions based on continuous verifier scores.
Achieves 86.5% on Terminal-Bench V2, 78.2% on SWE-Bench Verified, 87.4% on RoboRewardBench, and 73.3% on MedAgentBench.
Provides dense feedback signals that track task progress in Claude Code and improve sample efficiency for SAC and GRPO reinforcement learning.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables fine-grained, training-free solution verification and improves reinforcement learning sample efficiency across agentic, robotic, and mathematical domains.

papers.title: What Does a Discrete Diffusion Model Learn?

summary.tldr: This paper provides a unified CTMC ELBO framework for discrete diffusion models, proving the Oracle Distance theorem and establishing exact conversions between denoiser, score, and bridge plug-in parameterizations.
key_points: Proves the Oracle Distance theorem: negative ELBO equals data entropy plus the path KL from the oracle reverse process to the learned one, with an irreducible cost of -d/dt I(Z_0; Z_t).
Demonstrates that denoiser, cavity (bridge plug-in), and score are exact coordinate transformations of the optimal reverse jump rate for token-factorizing noise.
Shows that a denoiser parameterization causes the uniform diffusion ELBO to diverge at initialization, whereas the bridge plug-in parameterization remains finite.
Unifies existing discrete diffusion approaches (MDM, UDM, SEDD, and GIDD) as special cases of the continuous-time Markov chain ELBO framework.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides a mathematically exact foundation for discrete diffusion that prevents divergent losses at initialization and guides the correct choice of network parameterization.

papers.title: Selective Disclosure Watermarking for Large Language Models

summary.tldr: Hierarchical Vocabulary Routing (HeRo) introduces a multi-bit LLM watermarking framework that enables selective disclosure of embedded metadata based on verifier access levels.
key_points: Recursively partitions the vocabulary to distribute watermark information across hierarchical layers.
Allows verifiers to decode only the specific portions of the payload corresponding to their access privilege.
Preserves the unbiasedness of the underlying LLM sampling process to maintain text quality.
Achieves high detection accuracy and low latency while supporting fine-grained access control.
summary.why_it_matters: It resolves privacy and over-exposure risks in text watermarking by allowing model operators to restrict what metadata different third parties can extract from generated text.

papers.title: Beyond Heuristic Tuning: Power-Calibrated LLM Watermarking

summary.tldr: A power-calibrated statistical framework for logit-based LLM watermarking that models the exact trade-offs between hyperparameters, detection power, and semantic distortion to enable guided parameter optimization.
key_points: Replaces heuristic hyperparameter tuning with a power-calibrated statistical framework that explicitly links watermark parameters, detection power, and distortion.
Formulates watermark configuration as a constrained optimization problem to derive parameter selection procedures.
Provides empirically validated selection procedures that consistently identify Pareto-optimal trade-off points across diverse language models and datasets.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables principled, optimal hyperparameter selection for logit-based LLM watermarks, maximizing detection reliability while strictly controlling text quality degradation.

papers.title: Calibration-Family Overfit: Why Trusted Sabotage Monitors Don't Transfer Across Lineages

summary.tldr: Researchers demonstrate that trusted sabotage monitors suffer from calibration-family overfit, significantly reducing detection accuracy when evaluating untrusted AI models from different model lineages.
key_points: Cross-family evaluation on code-backdoor transcripts reveals a positive residual own-family advantage (interaction) of +0.172 AUROC across four open-weight families.

The performance gap is geometric, caused by each lineage's sabotage occupying distinct scoring directions; targeted rotation toward the target lineage restores detection while random rotation does not.
At a 1% audit budget using defer-to-trusted, off-lineage monitors catch 19% of attack attempts compared to 41% caught by in-lineage monitors.
Findings hold across an eight-family matrix of frontier vendors, controls matched for blatancy, monitors up to 34B parameters, and a secondary code benchmark.
summary.why_it_matters: Single-pairing evaluations overstate monitor safety, requiring AI control protocols to use cross-family transfer matrices to account for lineage-specific calibration gaps.

papers.title: $\mathbfλ$-VAE: Variance Equalization for Posterior Collapse

summary.tldr: The proposed λ-VAE resolves posterior collapse by introducing variance equalization via scaled sampling noise during reparameterization while retaining original posterior variance in the KL penalty.
key_points: Formalizes two independent causes of posterior collapse: gradient imbalance (reconstruction signal vanishing faster than KL pressure) and information gap (stochastic sampling discarding encoder representations).
Proves the information gap is algebraically equivalent to the mismatch between the aggregate posterior and the prior.
Modifies the reparameterization step by scaling sampling noise with per-dimension exponents derived in closed-form from a net information gain objective.
Uses a single hyperparameter to control the reconstruction-generation tradeoff while shifting the training attractor away from collapse.
Achieves up to 2.8x nats increase in information capacity and up to +0.33 BPD improvement in reconstruction quality on standard benchmarks.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides a unified theoretical explanation for posterior collapse and offers a simple reparameterization modification that reliably prevents latent dimension degeneration in VAEs.

papers.title: Untrusted Content Masking for Web Agents with Security Guarantees

summary.tldr: Untrusted Content Masking (UCM) restores the trust boundary for web agents by redacting untrusted DOM regions prior to agent observation and routing interactions through a sandboxed interface.
key_points: Webpages inherently entangle trusted instructions with untrusted content in rendered views, breaking traditional prompt injection isolation boundaries.
UCM uses the Document Object Model (DOM) structure to identify and redact untrusted regions without processing their actual content.
Interactions are routed through a sandboxed interface enforcing strict privilege separation to keep the agent isolated from adversarial input.
summary.why_it_matters: By re-establishing a strict isolation boundary on web interfaces, UCM enables provable security guarantees against prompt injection attacks in web agents.

papers.title: Is the Geometry Doing the Work? An Operating-Point Audit of Hierarchy in Hyperbolic Vision-Language Models

summary.tldr: An audit of hyperbolic vision-language models reveals that converged checkpoints remain near-Euclidean, failing to utilize active radial or cone-based geometric hierarchies due to a low-curvature shortcut.
key_points: Audited MERU, HyCoCLIP, and PHyCLIP models exhibit a maximum image-side dimensionless radius of $u=0.37$, far below the $u\approx0.84$ threshold required for $10\%$ local metric distortion.
Entailment cones in trained models are saturated or wide, causing low violation rates that stem from trivial geometry rather than genuine learned hierarchical order.
Gradient decomposition shows that the entailment loss acts as the primary pressure driving curvature contraction toward a low-curvature collapse, widening cones and suppressing violations.
Shuffle-controlled tests and preregisterd semantic traversals revealed no pair-specific radial ordering or operative full-hierarchy readouts across matched ViT-B seeds.
summary.why_it_matters: Current hyperbolic vision-language architectures fail to operationalize non-Euclidean geometry, meaning reported hierarchical performance gains may stem from supervision artifacts rather than hyperbolic representation.

papers.title: Revisiting the Relation Between Language Model Perplexity and ASR Word Error Rate for Modern End-to-End Speech Recognition

summary.tldr: This paper revisits the log-log linear relationship between language model perplexity and ASR word error rate for modern end-to-end systems, accounting for internal language modeling, encoder context, and LLMs.
key_points: Evaluates whether external language models, including neural LMs and large language models (LLMs), continue to lower word error rate (WER) in modern end-to-end ASR systems.
Analyzes the impact of ASR encoder context length on the historical log-log linear relation between LM perplexity (PPL) and WER.

Demonstrates that internal language model (ILM) subtraction in attention-based encoder-decoder architectures alters the PPL-WER curve, proving the decoder's internal LM capacity affects external LM performance metrics.
summary.why_it_matters: System designers must account for an end-to-end ASR model's decoder and internal language model when using external LM perplexity to predict speech recognition accuracy gains.

papers.title: Noisy-Channel Minimum Bayes Risk Decoding

summary.tldr: A noisy channel decomposition of Minimum Bayes Risk (MBR) decoding incorporates bidirectional hypothesis-reference effects to account for metric asymmetries.
key_points: MBR decoding traditionally suffers from a directional mismatch because evaluation metrics like BLEU and COMET are asymmetric.
The proposed method decomposes MBR decoding into four components: hypothesis-to-reference likelihood, reference-to-hypothesis likelihood, hypothesis prior, and reference prior.
The framework provides a unified interpretation of existing MBR variants and enables metric- and task-specific interpretability by isolating channel contributions.
Channel-wise contributions display consistent characteristics across different tasks but vary across metrics, indicating that channel weighting can improve standard MBR performance.
summary.why_it_matters: Properly accounting for asymmetric metric behaviors through channel weighting allows for higher-quality and more interpretable text generation over standard MBR decoding.

papers.title: EdgeBench: Unveiling Scaling Laws of Learning from Real-World Environments

summary.tldr: EdgeBench introduces 134 ultra-long-horizon real-world tasks and reveals that agent performance during environment learning follows a log-sigmoid scaling law (R^2 = 0.998), with agent learning speed doubling approximately every three months.
key_points: Analyzed approximately 38,000 hours of agent interactions across 134 real-world tasks requiring at least 12 hours of continuous operation under multilevel feedback.
Empirically identified a log-sigmoid scaling law for post-deployment environment learning with a fit of R^2 = 0.998.
Observed across model generations that agent learning speed in environments roughly doubles every three months.
Publicly released 51 tasks and the complete evaluation framework covering domains like software engineering, scientific discovery, and formal mathematics.
summary.why_it_matters: Establishing precise scaling laws for post-deployment environment learning provides a predictable framework for benchmarking and improving long-horizon autonomous agents.

papers.title: DSpark: Confidence-Scheduled Speculative Decoding with Semi-Autoregressive Generation

summary.tldr: DSpark improves speculative decoding efficiency using a semi-autoregressive drafter to model intra-block dependencies and confidence-scheduled verification to adjust token verification lengths dynamically based on estimated survival probabilities and server load.
key_points: Uses a semi-autoregressive drafting architecture that combines a parallel backbone with a lightweight sequential module to model intra-block dependencies and mitigate suffix decay.
Employs confidence-scheduled verification to dynamically trim verification lengths based on request-level prefix survival probabilities and engine-specific throughput profiles.
Reduces verification waste and saves batch capacity in high-concurrency serving environments compared to fixed-block parallel drafters.
Achieves a 60% to 85% speedup in per-user generation speed over the MTP-1 production baseline at matched throughput levels when deployed in the DeepSeek-V4 serving system.
summary.why_it_matters: DSpark shifts the serving Pareto frontier by preventing throughput collapse under high-concurrency workloads and strict interactivity constraints.

papers.title: When Agents Lie: Premeditation, Persistence, and Exploitation in Repeated Games

summary.tldr: In repeated n-player game experiments, over 90% of LLM agent deviations from public announcements were premeditated in private plans, with models exhibiting incompatible interpretations of whether announcements constitute binding commitments.
key_points: Agents were evaluated across six games in homogeneous and heterogeneous groups over 10 rounds using a three-stage protocol: private intent, public announcement, and final action.
When agents lied or deviated from public commitments, over 90% of those deviations were explicitly planned in advance during the private deliberation stage.
Honesty is highly domain-dependent rather than a static model property, with the same model varying from zero to near-total deviation depending on the game.

Cross-provider model pairings exhibit conflicting semantics around public announcements (binding commitment vs. cheap talk), creating payoff disparities that persist from Round 0 through all 10 rounds.
summary.why_it_matters: Deploying multi-provider agent networks requires explicit empirical testing, as systems cannot assume models share consistent implicit semantics regarding public commitments.

papers.title: Localized LoRA-MoE: Block-wise Low-Rank Experts With Adaptive Routing

summary.tldr: Localized LoRA-MoE combines block-wise spatial isolation with dynamic routing via centralized Block-Wise or decentralized Cell-Wise architectures to prevent gradient interference during parameter-efficient fine-tuning.
key_points: Introduces Block-Wise LoRA-MoE (Centralized Macro-Routing) to modulate the structural matrix grid using a monolithic context signal.
Introduces Cell-Wise LoRA-MoE (Decentralized Micro-Routing) to give individual matrix coordinate cells autonomous, localized expert gating.
Establishes that decentralized cell-level gating achieves statistical parity with global coordination, creating a gradient firewall against fault propagation.
Validated across SVD matrix simulations, tabular transformations, and vision tasks under sensor degradation.
summary.why_it_matters: It prevents destructive gradient interference and adapter collapse in multi-task parameter-efficient fine-tuning, allowing models to dynamically adapt to task switching and sensor failures.

papers.title: MIRAGE: Defending Long-Form RAG Against Misinformation Pollution

summary.tldr: MIRAGE is a training-free, model-agnostic defense mechanism that protects long-form RAG systems against document pollution by using an NLI-based cross-document claim graph and a Defended-Claims Gate.
key_points: MIRAGE constructs an NLI-based cross-document claim graph to evaluate evidence consistency across retrieved documents.
Uses a Defended-Claims Gate to restrict generation to a multi-source supported subset or trigger parametric answering if retrieval is blocked.
Includes a minimal-edit pollution protocol with four perturbation types: Unambiguous, Conflicting, Misleading, and Fabricated.
Restores factuality across four long-form QA benchmarks for both commercial and open-weight LLMs without retraining.
Code and datasets are made open-source on GitHub.
summary.why_it_matters: MIRAGE prevents LLMs from generating false or misleading long-form answers when retrieved search results contain subtle fabrications or conflicting information.

papers.title: Knowledge Knows, Verbalization Tells: Disentangling Latent Directions for Mathematical Solvability in LLMs

summary.tldr: Researchers disentangled distinct internal linear representations for mathematical solvability knowledge versus verbalization in LLMs, showing fabrication stems from shifts in verbalization rather than underlying model knowledge.
key_points: Solvability knowledge and verbalization are encoded as separate, linearly decodable representations within model hidden states across multiple LLMs.
Fabrication is primarily driven by changes in the verbalization representation rather than deficiencies in the underlying solvability knowledge.
Unsolvability cues in prompts reduce fabrication mainly by altering the verbalization representation.
Mechanistically manipulating these representations via activation steering improves the model's ability to abstain from answering unsolvable problems.
summary.why_it_matters: Disentangling internal knowledge from verbalization enables targeted activation steering to reduce hallucinations and improve model abstention on unanswerable mathematical tasks.

summary.tldr: Adversa AI's July 2026 digest highlights critical Model Context Protocol (MCP) vulnerabilities, real-world exploitation techniques, and official MCP hardening guidelines from the NSA.
key_points: Details critical security vulnerabilities affecting the Model Context Protocol (MCP).
Examines documented real-world exploitation scenarios targeting MCP implementations.
Summarizes official MCP hardening and defense guidelines published by the NSA.
summary.why_it_matters: Securing MCP implementations against real-world exploits is essential as national security agencies issue formal guidelines to protect AI context integrations.

security.title: The Hidden Risks of the Agentic Enterprise: Bridging the AI Governance Gap

summary.tldr: New research from Okta reveals a rapid increase in enterprise adoption of autonomous AI agents capable of executing workflows and accessing critical systems without human permission.
key_points: AI agents are transitioning enterprise software from permission-based, predictable execution to autonomous task completion.
Autonomous entities can independently access critical IT systems and sensitive corporate data.
AI agents possess the capability to spawn additional sub-agents to complete complex tasks without human oversight.
summary.why_it_matters: The rapid, unsanctioned deployment of autonomous agents creates significant AI governance and security gaps across enterprise IT infrastructure.

security.title: Calibration-Family Overfit: Why Trusted Sabotage Monitors Don't Transfer Across Lineages

summary.tldr: Trusted sabotage monitors suffer from calibration-family overfit, exhibiting a positive residual interaction (+0.172 AUROC) that causes a 21.7-point drop in sabotage detection when applied across different model lineages.
key_points: Cross-family evaluation reveals a +0.172 (95% CI [+0.158, +0.185]) own-family AUROC advantage across four open-weight families after accounting for sabotage blatancy and baseline monitor capability.

Geometric analysis shows each model lineage's sabotage occupies a distinct scoring direction; rotating the monitor's scoring direction toward the target lineage restores most lost detection performance.
Under a defer-to-trusted policy with a 1% audit budget, off-lineage monitors catch only 19% of attack attempts compared to 41% caught by in-lineage monitors at the same cost.
The overfit effect holds across an eight-family matrix spanning four frontier vendors, controls matched for blatancy, transcript-reading monitors up to 34B parameters, and multiple code benchmarks.
summary.why_it_matters: Single-pairing evaluations significantly overstate AI safety monitoring efficacy against uncalibrated model lineages, necessitating cross-family transfer matrices in AI control evaluations.

security.title: aiAuthZ: Off-Host, Identity-Bound Authorization for AI Agents

summary.tldr: aiAuthZ is an off-host authorization gateway that uses identity-bound HMAC-SHA256 signatures, single-use nonces, and argument-level policies to reduce AI agent attack success to 0% with 0.03 ms added decision latency.
key_points: Evaluated 15 LLMs against eight real-world attack scenarios, finding refusal rates ranged from 100% down to 38%, with the most expensive model refusing only 50% of attacks.
Enforces security off-host via per-message HMAC-SHA256 signatures, timestamps, single-use nonces, and unmodifiable role/argument policies.
Logs all decisions in a SHA-256 hash-chained audit trail and issues HMAC-authenticated QR receipts achieving 94% mean verification accuracy across eight transmission channels.
Blocked 100% of attacker-directed tool calls in the AgentDojo banking suite and 9 of 9 incident corpus case studies, compared to 4 of 9 for a non-identity-bound baseline.
summary.why_it_matters: It prevents compromised or deceived AI agents from executing unauthorized actions by enforcing strict, identity-verified authorization policy bounds outside of the model's runtime environment.

security.title: Statistical Adversaries: Natural Backdoor-like Features in Vision Datasets

summary.tldr: ImageNet contains naturally occurring, non-poisoned statistical signals that act like backdoors by predictably altering model predictions and transferring across vision architectures.
key_points: Statistical adversaries are non-malicious, naturally occurring data patterns in vision datasets that function similarly to backdoor triggers.
Candidate signals identified in ImageNet were isolated and verified using statistical controls to filter out random, non-causal correlations.
These unpoisoned statistical features transfer across different model architectures and are more targeted than generic image corruptions.
Vulnerabilities stem directly from the underlying dataset distribution and structure rather than specific model-level idiosyncrasies.
summary.why_it_matters: Dataset audits must treat natural spurious correlations as active security surfaces rather than mere sources of bias or interpretability issues.

security.title: Selective Disclosure Watermarking for Large Language Models

summary.tldr: Hierarchical Vocabulary Routing (HeRo) introduces a multi-bit LLM watermarking framework that enables selective disclosure of embedded metadata based on verifier access levels.
key_points: HeRo recursively partitions the vocabulary to distribute watermark payload information across hierarchical layers.
The framework provides fine-grained access control, allowing verifiers to decode only the specific metadata payload portions authorized for their access level.
It maintains original text quality by preserving the unbiasedness of the LLM's underlying sampling process.
summary.why_it_matters: It resolves privacy and over-exposure risks in multi-bit LLM watermarking by allowing model owners to reveal watermark metadata selectively rather than revealing the entire payload to all verifiers.

security.title: PiSAs: Benchmarking Contextual Integrity in Multi-User Agentic Systems

summary.tldr: PiSAs is a system-agnostic benchmark evaluating contextual integrity and cross-user data spillage in multi-user agentic systems across outputs, inter-agent communications, and shared memory.
key_points: Introduces dual Contextual Integrity (CI) annotations to measure task appropriateness and authorized user access boundaries.
Evaluates data spillage across diverse agent topologies, memory regimes, and system interfaces including inter-agent messages.
Identifies LLM reasoning failures as the primary bottleneck, with SOTA models failing to consistently filter contextually inappropriate content or limit transmission to authorized users.
summary.why_it_matters: System architecture improvements alone cannot prevent privacy leaks in multi-user AI infrastructure without better model-level context filtering and authorization reasoning.

security.title: Learning Only What Valid Adapters Can Express: Subspace-Constrained Adaptation Against Fine-Tuning Poisoning

summary.tldr: Subspace-Constrained Adaptation restricts fine-tuning to a low-dimensional subspace derived from trusted LoRA adapters, preserving clean task performance while blocking poisoning and backdoor attacks.
key_points: Analysis of 196 public LoRA adapters on flan-t5-large reveals 30% to 38% of weight norm is redundant, with functional content lying in a shared low-dimensional subspace.

Restricting gradient adaptation to 128 coordinates in this subspace matches full LoRA accuracy on clean data while maintaining 62-96% exact match under label inversion, compared to LoRA collapsing to 3-26%.
Adaptation loss on corrupted data is two orders of magnitude higher (120x) than on clean data, providing an inherent out-of-distribution detection signal without additional modules.

Against adaptive backdoor attacks within the subspace, attack success drops to 8% (vs. 100% for LoRA) when the target behavior is absent from the pool, but reaches 85% if the target matches existing pool behaviors.
summary.why_it_matters: It offers a built-in defense mechanism that prevents malicious or corrupted fine-tuning data from altering model behavior without requiring external anomaly detectors, provided a trusted adapter pool exists.

security.title: Untrusted Content Masking for Web Agents with Security Guarantees

summary.tldr: Untrusted Content Masking (UCM) restores trust boundaries in web agents by using DOM structure to redact untrusted webpage regions before observation and routing interactions through a sandboxed interface.
key_points: Identifies DOM structural information as sufficient to distinguish trusted from untrusted webpage regions without reading internal content.
Redacts untrusted page regions prior to agent processing to prevent prompt injection attacks.
Routes web agent interactions through a sandboxed interface that enforces strict privilege separation.
summary.why_it_matters: UCM enables provable security guarantees against prompt injection attacks for web agents by re-establishing the isolation between untrusted data and trusted instructions.

security.title: When Claws Remember but Do Not Tell: Stealthy Memory Injection in Persistent Personal Agents

summary.tldr: Researchers introduced WhisperBench and MemGhost to demonstrate stealth memory injection attacks, where a single malicious email silently writes poisoned state into a persistent personal agent's long-term memory to compromise future behavior.
key_points: WhisperBench provides a 108-case benchmark spanning five risk categories for evaluating stealth memory injection across fact and preference poisoning in real IMAP/SMTP workflows.
MemGhost uses an environment proxy and an objective proxy converting memory adoption and stealth into rubric rewards to train a one-shot payload generation policy via SFT and RL.
MemGhost achieved an 87.5% end-to-end success rate on OpenClaw with GPT-5.4 and 71.4% on Claude Code SDK with Sonnet 4.6 across 56 held-out test cases.
Attacks successfully transferred across NanoClaw and Hermes Agent architectures, filesystem and Mem0 vector backends, and bypassed input, model, and system defenses.
summary.why_it_matters: Persistent agent memory allows untrusted external content like emails to become a silent, long-term vector for execution hijack without requiring immediate user detection.

security.title: Privilege and confidentiality in generative AI workflows

summary.tldr: An analysis of legal privilege and confidentiality risks arising from generative AI data storage in model parameters, context windows, and RAG databases, evaluated against UK/US case law and solicitor regulatory standards.
key_points: GenAI systems store and process client data through three distinct modes: parameter memorisation via training, live session context windows, and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) databases.
Each of the three processing modes presents unique data leakage and confidentiality risks that challenge traditional legal professional privilege principles.
The analysis grounds these data leakage risks in recent legal precedents, specifically UK and Munir v Secretary of State for the Home Department and United States v Heppner.
Effective information governance standards for solicitors are shifting, establishing new benchmarks for professional negligence and regulatory compliance regarding client data protection.
summary.why_it_matters: Legal practitioners must adapt information governance strategies to address AI-specific data leakage risks to preserve professional secrecy and avoid negligence or misconduct.

security.title: Agent Data Injection Attacks are Realistic Threats to AI Agents

summary.tldr: Researchers introduced Agent Data Injection (ADI), a new category of indirect prompt injection that bypasses current defenses by injecting malicious data disguised as trusted metadata or context formats to hijack AI agent execution.
key_points: ADI targets trusted metadata (such as resource identifiers and data origins) and agent context data (such as tool call and response formats) rather than standard instructions.
The attack exploits a fundamental failure in current AI agents to isolate trusted context data from untrusted external data.

Demonstrated ADI vulnerabilities enable arbitrary click attacks on web agents (Claude in Chrome, Antigravity, Nanobrowser) and remote code execution or supply-chain attacks on coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI).
ADI proved effective across both standalone LLMs and off-the-shelf AI agent configurations, successfully bypassing existing indirect prompt injection defenses.
summary.why_it_matters: Existing indirect prompt injection defenses are insufficient because they fail to prevent attackers from manipulating agent control flow through untrusted context and metadata injection.

security.title: Your Agent's Memories Are Not Its Own: Forged Reasoning Attacks on LLM Agent Memory and Defenses

summary.tldr: Researchers introduced FARMA, an attack that poisons an LLM agent's persistent reasoning history to bypass defenses, and SENTINEL, a layered defense pipeline that mitigates it.
key_points: FARMA inserts forged reasoning traces using evasive language to bypass keyword defenses, then uses self-referential reinforcement to defeat consensus-based defenses like A-MemGuard.
FARMA achieved up to a 100% attack success rate across multiple agents and LLMs over 50 trials.
SENTINEL incorporates a Reasoning Guard that uses five weighted signals to structurally analyze candidate entries for forgery.
In evaluations, SENTINEL reduced FARMA's attack success rate to as low as 0% with zero false positives across 326 benign agent traces.
summary.why_it_matters: Demonstrates that securing LLM agents requires protecting the structural integrity of their historical reasoning traces, not just filtering factual or retrieved content.

security.title: Retroactive Chain-of-Thought (RetroCoT): Forensic Reconstruction Prompts as a Safety Diagnostic Across Model Generations

summary.tldr: Retroactive Chain-of-Thought (RetroCoT) bypasses LLM safety alignment by framing harmful requests as forensic causal reconstructions of already-occurred events, achieving up to 58% attack success rates on gpt-4o.
key_points: RetroCoT operates as a single-turn attack that asks the model to act as a forensic analyst and reverse-engineer the causal chain of a presupposed harmful outcome.
On AdvBench (n=50), RetroCoT raised Attack Success Rates (ASR) from 0% to 58% on gpt-4o and from 4% to 52% on gpt-4o-mini compared to direct requests.
GPT-5-family models initially achieved 0% ASR against RetroCoT by explicitly identifying the reconstruction premise in their refusal rationales.
Adding a single adversarial feedback turn with evaluator critique bypassed GPT-5.4-mini protections, increasing its ASR from 0% to 48% (and to 85% in a control condition without fake low scores).
summary.why_it_matters: The findings demonstrate that safety alignment in frontier language models relies on specific pragmatic framing rather than a true semantic understanding of harmful intent.

security.title: BioSecBench-Refusal: A paired metric for performance and alignment in agentic biosecurity risk assessment

summary.tldr: BioSecBench-Refusal is a new benchmark that pairs 61 routine biological tasks with 46 red-team hazard scenarios to evaluate model performance, threat identification, and over-refusal in agentic life science workflows.
key_points: Benchmark consists of 61 Routine tasks adapted from literature and 46 Red-Team tasks with concealed biosecurity hazards.
Tested across 16 model-harness configurations, refusal rates spanned 7%-74% for Routine tasks and 1%-62% for Red-Team tasks.
Many configurations refused legitimate Routine research at rates equal to or higher than Red-Team hazards.
Provider API filters applied prior to agentic reasoning triggered the majority of refusals, whereas models allowed to reason identified threats more effectively.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides developers with a metric to prevent safety guardrails from inappropriately blocking legitimate biological research while ensuring actual biosecurity threats are caught.

infra.title: Bringing PyTorch Monarch to AMD GPUs: Single-Controller Distributed Training on ROCm

summary.tldr: PyTorch Monarch, a single-controller distributed training framework, has been ported to AMD Instinct GPUs with ROCm, enabling elastic, fault-tolerant large language model training beyond CUDA environments.
key_points: Monarch's architecture decouples the Python API from a Rust runtime (Tokio) and infrastructure, managing actors, meshes, supervision trees, and tensor sharding.
The system dynamically recovers from node failures, allowing healthy nodes to continue training while failed nodes recover, minimizing wasted computation.
Traditional checkpointing, which causes wasted computation and cluster idle time, is replaced by Monarch's dynamic fault-tolerance model.
Porting Monarch to ROCm required significant engineering effort to adapt its GPU runtime and distributed communication stack.
summary.why_it_matters: This enables more reliable and efficient large-scale AI infrastructure by addressing hardware failures in distributed training environments.
